A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments measuring explanation approximation errors, feature rankings, distribution discrepancies and computational costs across tabular, image and text datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical benchmarks and adds statistical test results and detailed explanation case studies in Appendix I.

M1.justification: CTE still uses COMPRESS++ with a Gaussian kernel to select samples before applying existing explanation estimators. Listings 1–4 retain the same procedures; the revised theoretical justification does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same five OpenXAI datasets, 48 OpenML tasks, and IMDB/ImageNet experiments. Appendix I uses existing datasets; its additional model configurations and explanation examples do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain i.i.d. sampling and k-medoids clustering as comparators, with unchanged participation across the retained comparisons. The new case studies compare CTE against the existing i.i.d. baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds case-study configurations including XGBoost on COMPAS and a convolutional network on CIFAR-10. The earlier benchmark specifies an OpenXAI neural network for COMPAS and a fully connected network for CIFAR-10. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, metrics and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds visual error analyses for SAGE, SHAP, feature effects and expected gradients, including correctly and incorrectly classified CIFAR-10 examples. These supplement the retained sample-size and foreground/background ablations and the existing G-LIME analysis.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 adds Welch's t-tests for expected-gradient improvements on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, reporting p < 1e-10. Both versions still specify 33 sampling repetitions and three ground-truth estimation repetitions; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Appendix I adds concrete case-study results, such as COMPAS Kernel-SAGE MAE of 0.0050 for i.i.d. sampling versus 0.0011 for CTE in Figure 25, plus individual CIFAR-10 attribution errors. The retained benchmark plots and aggregate rankings are unchanged; Table 1 mainly summarizes existing results.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the TV-based Propositions 3.4–3.5 and MMD–TV Lemma 3.6 with direct biased-MMD bounds in Propositions 1–2. It introduces a KDE-based MMD definition, changes the global error bound from L1 to L2, and replaces Appendix B with two Cauchy–Schwarz proofs.

C1.justification: v1 presents CTE primarily as an empirically supported approach with qualified theoretical intuition. v2's abstract and contribution statement elevate a discovered theoretical connection and theoretical justification to a central contribution. The main empirical accuracy and sample-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly warns that its MMD-to-explanation intuition admits counterexamples. v2 removes that qualification and interprets its new bounds as direct control of explanation error through MMD minimization. It also adds Gaussian-kernel rationale and warns that aggregate SHAP visualizations can conceal individual attribution errors.

D1.justification: Reported cluster computation changes from approximately 12 days in v1 Appendix D.3 to 14 days in v2 Appendix H, with the same hardware. Implementation listings, principal hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions and disclosed code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references on attribution methods and MMD theory, and discusses supervised kernel thinning by Gong et al. and influence functions by Koh and Liang. These extend the context without substantially replacing the existing related-work positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and theoretical narrative are substantially rewritten. Explanation-accuracy experiments now lead Section 4, distribution-compression analysis moves later, preliminaries gain subsections, and the conclusion becomes an expanded discussion. The appendices gain a contents page and separate compute-resources section.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, existing main figures gain panel labels and efficiency annotations, and v2 adds summary Table 1 and Figures 25–31. The retained appendix benchmark plots are largely rescaled and relocated.

improvement.justification: The summaries, significance tests and case studies improve presentation, but the theoretical justification becomes less reliable. Unlike v1's qualified TV-based intuition, v2 promotes direct MMD guarantees whose proofs incorrectly infer integral L2 bounds from pointwise boundedness (Appendix B, Eqs. 6–7 and 13–14), without the necessary additional assumptions. This overstatement outweighs the reporting gains, although the empirical contribution remains intact.
